capability_investigated:
The feature-extraction + batched-decode path: processor() always pads/
truncates audio to one 30s (3000-frame) mel window, and generate() accepts a
batched feature view (N,80,3000) paired with one prompt per item.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor() call hard-caps coverage at the first 30s, so on
multi-minute 0715 calls almost the entire reference is deleted (length_ratio
floored). generate() decodes N stacked windows in a single call, so full-file
coverage costs one batched decode per file rather than N sequential calls.
hypothesis:
Slice audio into consecutive 30s windows, stack their mel features, decode the
whole batch at once, and join the per-window text. This directly attacks the
dominant deletion axis by transcribing the tail the stub threw away, while the
batched call keeps runtime inside the budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs GPU memory: how peak CUDA allocation scales
with the number of stacked (80,3000) mel windows passed in one decode call.
what_i_learned:
generate() does NOT stream the batch — passing all N windows of a multi-minute
file as one (N,80,3000) view makes the whole batch resident on the GPU at once
and OOMs. The batch dimension is bounded by VRAM, not just by API acceptance;
one-window-per-call keeps peak memory flat at single-window size.
hypothesis:
Keep the full-file 30s windowing that fixes the deletion/length_ratio floor,
but decode each window in its own generate() call instead of one batched call,
so coverage no longer trades against an OOM crash.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_size decoding kwarg on the per-window decode path — how the
CT2 Whisper search width changes within-window coverage versus the greedy
(beam_size=1) decode the parent uses.
what_i_learned:
The parent already covers the full audio (every 30s window is decoded), yet
length_ratio is only 0.65 and repeated_text fires on 4/12 files. So the
deletion is intra-window, not coverage-of-audio: greedy beam=1 decode collapses
into repetition loops / early EOS inside a window and strands the rest of that
window's speech. CT2 generate() does NOT auto-fallback on temperature, so beam
width is the available robustness lever against greedy collapse.
hypothesis:
Raise beam_size 1->5 on the per-window decode. Wider beam search avoids the
greedy looping/early-termination that deletes the tail of each window, lifting
length_ratio and cutting repeated_text against the dominant deletion axis;
~5x of 103.8s inference still fits the 719.9s budget.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return object beyond sequences_ids — the return_scores and
return_no_speech_prob decoding kwargs, and what WhisperGenerationResult
exposes (scores = length-normalised log-prob of the chosen hypothesis,
no_speech_prob) that the pipeline currently discards.
what_i_learned:
generate() will populate result.scores (a length-normalised mean log-prob,
reference-comparable to Whisper's avg_logprob ~-1.0 threshold) and
no_speech_prob when asked, so the decoder's own confidence is readable per
window. Combined with gzip compression ratio of the decoded text, that gives
the exact two-signal degeneracy test Whisper uses — meaning manual
temperature fallback (which iter_003 found CT2 does NOT do automatically) is
fully implementable on the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
Intra-window collapse (iter_003: repetition loops / early EOS strand a
window's tail → deletion 82%) is curable by re-decoding only the degenerate
windows at escalating temperature. Gate retries on scores < -1.0 OR
compression_ratio > 2.4 so healthy windows stay at one beam=5 decode; failing
windows escalate T=0→1.0 with full-vocab sampling, recovering stranded speech
and raising length_ratio without inflating runtime.

capability_investigated:
result.no_speech_prob on the WhisperGenerationResult — already populated via
return_no_speech_prob=True since iter_004 but never read — as Whisper's
reference non-speech detector, paired with result.scores[0].
what_i_learned:
family_002 and family_001 share the beam=5 base; family_002's only added
mechanism (temperature fallback) is precisely what raised hallucination
0.18→0.27, because on near-silent windows it escalates to full-distribution
sampling (topk=0) and hallucinates. no_speech_prob is the discarded signal
that flags those windows before escalation, so the deletion-recovery of
family_002 and the lower-hallucination behaviour of family_001 can coexist:
detect degeneracy via compression+logprob, but gate the sampling escalation
behind a silence check.
hypothesis:
Graft both: keep family_002's beam=5 + compression/logprob temperature
fallback (deletion axis), and guard the hallucination axis it regressed by
returning "" when no_speech_prob > 0.6 AND scores[0] < -1.0 — Whisper's exact
non-speech rule — so silent windows are skipped instead of sampled into
invented text. Conservative thresholds keep speech-heavy high-deletion files
(length_ratio 0.51–0.58, low no_speech) untouched.

capability_investigated:
Whisper timestamp tokens on the generate() path: removing <|notimestamps|>
from the prompt so result.sequences_ids carries <|t|> tokens (ids >=
convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), 0.02s steps), and what the last
segment-end timestamp says about how far the 30s window was consumed.
what_i_learned:
The frozen surface supports timestamp decoding: the prompt without
<|notimestamps|> lets the model emit timestamp tokens in sequences_ids, and
their value (id - timestamp_begin) * 0.02 gives the consumed-time of each
window — a per-window seek signal the fixed-stride pipeline never had.
length_ratio sits at ~0.65 on EVERY file (even flagless ones, e.g. 0.81/0.74
best-cases), so the deletion is a systematic boundary loss from blind 30s
cuts, not just the degenerate-window collapse iter_003 isolated.
hypothesis:
Decode with timestamps and advance the next window to the last segment-end
timestamp instead of a blind +30s. Utterances straddling a boundary are then
re-decoded whole from the next window's start rather than truncated, lifting
coverage/length_ratio against the dominant deletion axis; healthy windows
reaching ~30s still take a full stride so added decode cost is bounded.

capability_investigated:
The two generate() calls in _decode_window and which of their return-value
flags the gating logic actually consumes: result.scores[0] (logprob) and the
gzip compression ratio of the decoded text are read; result.no_speech_prob,
populated by return_no_speech_prob=True, is never read anywhere.
what_i_learned:
return_no_speech_prob=True is a pure dead override on the mature pipeline:
it populates result.no_speech_prob but the degeneracy gate uses only
compression_ratio<=2.4 AND avg_logprob>=-1.0. Requesting it cannot change
sequences_ids or text, so removing it is CER-neutral by construction — the
signal iter_005 proposed gating on was never actually wired in.
hypothesis:
ABLATE: remove return_no_speech_prob=True from both generate() calls. The
decode output and gating are unchanged, so CER holds while the call surface
is simpler and one unused per-window return computation is dropped.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s prompts argument as a writable input, not just the fixed
[sot, lang, task] triple — specifically the <|startofprev|> token slot that
Whisper reserves before <|startoftranscript|> for previous-text conditioning
(condition_on_previous_text), and whether CT2 honors arbitrary prepended ids.
what_i_learned:
The prompt is a flat token-id list fully under workspace control: prepending
[startofprev, *prev_text_tokens, sot, lang, task] is accepted by generate()
and conditions the decode on prior context. This is an input-side lever
distinct from every prior finding (all of which read decode *outputs* —
scores, no_speech_prob, timestamps — or widened search). It directly targets
substitution, which coverage/timestamp work cannot, since it changes *what*
the decoder recognizes (domain terms, cross-boundary continuations) rather
than how much audio is consumed.
hypothesis:
With length_ratio healthy (0.96) and substitution now 56% of error, prime each
window with the running call context via <|startofprev|> + the last 224 text
tokens, reset after a degeneracy-gate failure so a repetition loop cannot
poison later prompts. Consistent domain vocabulary across the ~80 windows/file
should lower substitution without affecting coverage.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s no_repeat_ngram_size decoding kwarg — a logit-processor-level
constraint applied during the search step that hard-bans re-emitting any
n-gram already produced in the hypothesis. Distinct from the compression-ratio
health check, which only detects a repetition loop after it has already been
decoded and then pays for a full temperature-fallback re-decode.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface exposes decode-time repetition control, not just
the post-hoc detect-and-redecode path the pipeline uses now. no_repeat_ngram_size
is an unused logit constraint orthogonal to beam_size (search width), the
temperature schedule (sampling), timestamps (coverage), and the prompt slot
(input conditioning) — it shapes the per-step distribution so a verbatim loop
cannot form, rather than scoring a finished hypothesis. This is the first
in-search robustness lever probed; all prior findings read outputs or widened
search after the fact.
hypothesis:
Banning repeated trigrams (size 3) on both the beam and sampling decode calls
should clear the repeated_text guard violations on focus files 1065 and 8016
before the compression gate ever fires, removing the repetition-driven
insertions/substitutions inside those loops while leaving healthy windows
(where exact trigram repeats are rare in natural Korean call speech) untouched.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam-search `patience` decoding kwarg on the temperature=0.0
path — distinct from beam_size (search width, probed iter_003). Patience is
the CT2/Whisper factor controlling how many finished hypotheses the beam
search collects (≈ beam_size * patience) before finalizing, i.e. how long
alternative beams stay alive before the best is committed.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface accepts `patience` independently of beam_size,
so beam exploration depth is tunable without widening the beam itself. This
is an in-search hypothesis-selection lever (orthogonal to width, sampling,
timestamps, prompt slot, and no_repeat_ngram) — the relevant axis for
substitution, which is decided by *which* completed hypothesis wins, not by
how much audio is consumed (length_ratio already healthy at 0.96).
hypothesis:
On the parent (family_003, beam=5, no_speech ablated), raising patience to
2.0 lets the beam search evaluate roughly twice as many completed candidates
before committing, surfacing a higher-scoring transcription on noisy
phone-band Korean audio and lowering the dominant substitution error without
affecting coverage or the sampling-fallback path.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses decoding kwarg and the multi-entry shape of the
return object it produces: result.sequences_ids and result.scores become
parallel N-long lists (the top-N completed beam hypotheses, score-ranked),
not the single-best [0] entry the pipeline has always read. Distinct from
beam_size (search WIDTH, iter_003) and patience (exploration DEPTH, iter_010)
— this is the first probe of the search's *output multiplicity*.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface can return the whole N-best beam list, not just
the argmax hypothesis. Every prior search-side finding (beam, patience,
no_repeat_ngram) consumed only sequences_ids[0]; with num_hypotheses=N the
caller sees the alternative completed beams and their per-hypothesis scores,
giving an in-search degeneracy escape: pick the highest-ranked beam that
passes the compression+logprob health checks. This is reachable WITHOUT the
temperature sampling that iter_005 identified as the hallucination source.
hypothesis:
Request num_hypotheses=5 on the beam (temp=0.0) decode and return the first
N-best hypothesis that clears the two health checks, falling back to the
score-top beam, and only escalating temperature when no beam is clean. Because
the dominant degeneracy on the two flagged files (repeated_text, hallucination)
is a single bad top beam, swapping in a clean sibling beam should cut those
hits without the sampling-induced hallucination cost — at no extra decode for
windows whose top beam is already clean.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s repetition_penalty decoding kwarg — a soft per-step multiplicative
logit penalty on tokens already present in the running hypothesis, applied
inside the beam search. Distinct from no_repeat_ngram_size (iter_009, a hard
in-search ban of repeated n-grams) and from the compression-ratio health check
(a post-hoc detector that pays a full temperature-fallback re-decode only after
a loop has finished forming).
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface carries TWO independent in-search repetition
controls, not one: the hard n-gram ban (no_repeat_ngram_size) probed in iter_009
and a soft global repetition_penalty that scales down the logit of any
previously-emitted token without forbidding it outright. The soft penalty can
damp a forming verbatim loop while still allowing genuine short repeats, which
a hard ban cannot. It is a per-step shaping lever orthogonal to beam width
(iter_003), patience (iter_010), num_hypotheses (iter_011), and the prompt slot
(iter_008) — and complementary to the compression gate, which only acts after
the loop is already decoded.
hypothesis:
Two focus_files flag repeated_text (1065…, 8016…) that the compression-ratio
gate at 2.4 never trips, so their repeated content survives into the output and
inflates error. Adding a mild repetition_penalty=1.1 to both decode paths
discourages the loop from forming during the beam=5 temp=0 pass rather than
relying on a post-hoc redecode, lowering the repeated/inserted text those long
files accumulate while staying gentle enough not to suppress legitimate Korean
repetition.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s length_penalty decoding kwarg on the deterministic beam_size=5
path — the exponent in CT2's length normalization score = sum(logprob) /
(length ** length_penalty), which controls how completed beams are reranked
before the best is committed. Distinct from beam_size (search WIDTH, iter_003),
patience (exploration DEPTH, iter_010), num_hypotheses (output MULTIPLICITY,
iter_011), and the two repetition controls (iter_009/012).
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface exposes a beam-reranking lever orthogonal to
every search knob probed so far: length_penalty changes the final score used
to pick the winning completed hypothesis, not the search trajectory. With the
default exponent of 1.0 the normalization divides by raw length; raising it
shifts the argmax toward fuller hypotheses among the existing 5 beams. This is
the relevant axis for substitution (56% dominant, length_ratio already healthy
at 0.96) because the error is decided by WHICH completed beam wins, not by how
much audio is consumed.
hypothesis:
Set length_penalty=1.1 on the temperature=0.0 beam path so the beam reranker
favors the fuller, less-truncated hypothesis among the 5 completed beams,
changing which domain-term spelling the decode commits to and shaving the
dominant substitution axis without adding any decode cost.

capability_investigated:
The audio input to processor()'s feature extractor — the signal level the
WhisperProcessor turns into log-mel before generate() ever runs. Studied how
HF's WhisperFeatureExtractor maps amplitude to features: it applies a fixed
affine log-mel offset ((log_spec + 4.0) / 4.0) with NO data-dependent
amplitude normalization, so the raw input level passes straight through to the
encoder's mel magnitudes.
what_i_learned:
Input signal level is an un-conditioned surface: because the feature extractor
does not normalize amplitude, two recordings of the same speech at different
gains produce different mel energies and thus different encoder activations.
The 0715 batch spans ~16 dB of mean RMS file-to-file (-26 to -41 dB), so quiet
phone-band calls reach the encoder under-driven. Every prior iteration acted on
decode outputs/search/prompt; none conditioned the input level, making this a
genuinely unused lever — and the only one that touches acoustics rather than
search, which is where substitution (56%, length_ratio healthy 0.96) lives.
hypothesis:
Peak-normalize each file once to a fixed target (0.95) using a robust 99.9th
percentile of |audio| (not the max sample, to ignore transient clicks) before
windowing. A single global gain levels the file without amplifying the noise
floor of silence-heavy windows. If under-driven mels are an acoustic source of
the dominant substitution error, consistent input level should let the encoder
resolve domain vocabulary it currently mis-recognizes on quiet calls.

capability_investigated:
Composition of two prior input-side levers on the mature timestamp-seek
pipeline: the WhisperProcessor feature extractor's un-normalized amplitude
path (iter_014) and generate()'s writable prompt prefix via the
<|startofprev|> token slot for previous-text conditioning (iter_008).
what_i_learned:
The two input-side levers are independent and composable: peak-normalization
acts on mel magnitudes before the encoder (acoustic), while the
<|startofprev|> prompt prefix conditions the decoder's token distribution
(textual context). Neither touches search/coverage, and the clean-gate that
iter_008 needed (drop prev-text after a degeneracy-tripped window) is already
available as the compression+logprob break in _decode_window — so threading a
`clean` flag out of it wires both gains without new decode calls.
hypothesis:
Stacking acoustic leveling (under-driven quiet calls hurt recognition) with
running-context priming (consistent domain vocab + cross-boundary
continuation) attacks the dominant substitution axis (56%, length_ratio 0.96)
from both the acoustic and lexical sides at once, where each alone improved
the sub share but not overall CER.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s prompt argument used as a STATIC domain-prime in the
<|startofprev|> slot (the slot itself was found in iter_008): tokenizing a
fixed Korean insurance-call-center glossary via tokenizer.encode(...,
add_special_tokens=False) and prepending [startofprev, *glossary, sot, lang,
task] on EVERY window, rather than carrying the previous window's decoded text.
what_i_learned:
The prompt slot accepts arbitrary pre-tokenized text, so it can carry a fixed
curated lexicon instead of rolling decoded text. This decouples the iter_008
conditioning mechanism from its failure mode: iter_008's prev-text drifts and
poisons later windows once one degenerates (which is why it regressed), but a
static glossary has no carryover, primes the first window too, and is identical
across files — making it a clean substitution-targeted prime with no degeneracy
coupling and no extra decode calls.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (56%, length_ratio healthy 0.96) and lives in
mis-recognized domain terms / phone-band homophones. Priming each window with a
fixed insurance glossary (보험료/약관/계약자/특약/해약환급금 …) biases the decoder
toward the correct spellings of exactly those terms, lowering substitution
without the poisoning that sank rolling prev-text and without touching search,
sampling, coverage, or input level.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s sampling_topp (nucleus) decoding kwarg on the temperature-fallback
branch of _decode_window. Distinct from sampling_topk (which the fallback pins
to 0 = full distribution) and from sampling_temperature (the escalation schedule
itself). This is the candidate-set-shape lever on the sampler, never set before.
what_i_learned:
The frozen generate() surface exposes sampling_topp, so the temperature-fallback
sampler's candidate set is independently controllable from its temperature. The
current fallback uses sampling_topk=0, meaning it draws from the ENTIRE vocab
distribution at every escalated temperature — iter_005 already identified this
exact full-distribution draw as the hallucination source on low-confidence
windows. topp lets the fallback stay a degeneracy-escape (temperature still
diversifies among the top beams) without exposing the deep tail.
hypothesis:
Add sampling_topp=0.9 to the fallback generate() call. The fallback fires only on
windows that failed the compression+logprob gate (the hardest audio), and its
topk=0 full-distribution sampling there draws off-distribution tail tokens that
surface as hallucinated substitutions/insertions (hal 0.18). Restricting draws to
the 0.9-mass nucleus keeps the escape from a repetition loop but removes the tail,
so the same window resolves to on-distribution text instead of garbage — targeting
the hallucination axis (and the substitutions it inflates) at zero extra decode cost.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s supported sampler kwargs, read from the TypeError signature dump
that crashed iter_017: the only accepted sampling levers are sampling_topk
(int) and sampling_temperature (float). sampling_topp is not in the binding.
what_i_learned:
sampling_topp (nucleus) is NOT available on the frozen CT2 surface — passing
it raises TypeError before any decode runs, which is exactly what failed
iter_017. Candidate-set shaping on the fallback sampler is therefore only
reachable through a finite sampling_topk; topk=0 means full-vocab draw.
hypothesis:
Achieve iter_017's intent with the supported lever: replace the fallback's
sampling_topk=0 (full distribution, iter_005's hallucination source) with a
finite sampling_topk=10, so escalation still escapes a degenerate beam but
cannot reach the off-distribution tail that produces hallucinated subs.

capability_investigated:
result.no_speech_prob on the WhisperGenerationResult (populated by
return_no_speech_prob=True on both generate() calls) as Whisper's reference
non-speech detector, and the temperature-escalation control flow in
_decode_window that currently ignores it.
what_i_learned:
no_speech_prob is a live per-window float on the beam result but is consumed
nowhere (iter_007 confirmed it dead); the degeneracy gate uses only
compression_ratio and avg_logprob. So a near-silent window fails the logprob
check and escalates into topk=0 sampling, which is exactly where it
hallucinates/loops. Wiring the reference rule (skip when no_speech_prob>0.6
AND avg_logprob<-1.0, confident decode overrides) short-circuits that path
before escalation, costs no extra decode, and only fires on low-confidence
non-speech windows.
hypothesis:
Gate the temperature escalation behind the no_speech_prob silence check in
_decode_window: on the beam pass, if no_speech_prob exceeds 0.6 and
avg_logprob is below -1.0, return empty text immediately instead of
escalating to full-distribution sampling. This suppresses the silence-window
hallucination/repetition that drives the two repeated_text 0715 files and the
0.18 hallucination rate, while the avg_logprob override preserves genuine
quiet phone-band speech.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s suppress_tokens decoding kwarg — a hard logit-level token ban
applied during the CT2 beam/sampling search, zeroing the probability of the
listed ids at every step. Distinct from suppress_blank, from the search knobs
(beam_size/patience/num_hypotheses), from both repetition controls
(no_repeat_ngram_size hard ban, repetition_penalty soft), and from the
post-hoc compression/logprob gate that only re-decodes after degeneracy.
what_i_learned:
The frozen surface lets the caller constrain the *output alphabet*, not just
search shape: by decoding each non-special, non-timestamp vocab id
(tokenizer.all_special_ids excluded, ids < timestamp_begin) and testing its
characters against script-block ranges, the multilingual model's entire
foreign-script subspace (CJK ideographs incl. Hanja, kana, Cyrillic, Greek,
Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Devanagari) can be enumerated and passed to
suppress_tokens. This is an in-search constraint orthogonal to all prior
levers; it targets substitution directly (length_ratio already healthy 0.96)
by removing cross-script homophone targets a Korean-only batch can never need.
hypothesis:
The dominant 56% substitution includes the model resolving phone-band Korean
syllables into homophonic wrong-script tokens (e.g. a 漢字 or kana the
reference never contains). Banning the foreign-script vocab at logit time
forces the argmax onto in-vocabulary Hangul/Latin/digit tokens during search,
so the substitution cannot form — unlike a post-hoc gate, which can only
detect and re-decode after the wrong token is already committed.

capability_investigated:
The transcript-assembly stage (`" ".join(texts)`), i.e. how per-window decoded
strings are merged into the final return value — distinct from every prior probe,
which touched decode inputs (prompt slot, level), search knobs (beam/patience/
num_hypotheses/penalties/suppress), or decode outputs (scores/no_speech/timestamps).
Nothing in the ledger acts on the assembled text after decoding.
what_i_learned:
The pipeline does zero post-decode text processing: decoded window strings are
concatenated raw. A repetition loop that compresses just under the 2.4 gate, or
one that re-forms across a timestamp-seek seam, therefore survives verbatim into
the final string as pure insertion error — this is the mechanism behind the two
`repeated_text` guard-violation focus files (1065, 8016) and the 0.18 repeated
rate, none of which the in-search controls fully suppressed.
hypothesis:
Add `_collapse_repeats`: scan the assembled word list and reduce any contiguous
run where a 1–4 word phrase repeats ≥3× to a single occurrence, then return the
collapsed text. This strips degenerate loops that the compression gate misses,
cutting insertions and clearing the repeated_text guard, while being CER-neutral
on non-looping files (natural Korean call speech does not triple an eojeol phrase).

capability_investigated:
Composition of two independent input-side substitution levers on the mature
timestamp-seek pipeline: the WhisperProcessor feature extractor's
un-normalized amplitude path (iter_014, acoustic) and generate()'s writable
prompt prefix via the <|startofprev|> slot loaded with a STATIC domain
glossary rather than rolling prev-text (iter_016, textual).
what_i_learned:
The acoustic level lever and the static-glossary prompt lever are fully
composable and orthogonal: peak-normalization rescales mel magnitudes before
the encoder while the <|startofprev|> glossary conditions the decoder token
distribution, and neither touches search or coverage. The earlier
level+prompt composition (iter_015) paired level-norm with ROLLING prev-text
— which carries iter_008's drift/poison failure — whereas the static glossary
has no carryover, so this pairing combines the two cleanest sub-improvers
(iter_014 sub +0.04/hal +0.09; iter_016 sub-targeted, drift-free) without
reintroducing the degeneracy coupling that sank iter_015.
hypothesis:
Substitution (56%, length_ratio healthy 0.96) has two un-combined input-side
reducers; applying both at once — per-file peak-normalization plus a fixed
insurance-domain glossary in the prompt prefix on every window — attacks the
dominant axis from acoustic and textual directions simultaneously, which
neither alone could win on, while leaving coverage and the degeneracy gate
untouched.

capability_investigated:
The raw `audio` numpy input as a segmentation substrate (not the forbidden
audio_profile assets): computing a per-frame RMS envelope over each 30s window
and locating inter-utterance silence to place the window boundary, versus the
iter_006 mechanism that places it from decode-output timestamp tokens. First
probe of input-side window placement; all prior segmentation work read decode
OUTPUTS (sequences_ids timestamps), never the signal.
what_i_learned:
Window boundaries can be placed before any decode runs: a relative gate
(frame RMS < 0.2 * the window's own RMS) is level-agnostic across the batch's
16 dB RMS spread (-26 to -41 dB) and reliably marks silence frames, and most
windows have a silence gap in the [24s,30s] tail band (median speech segment
is 2-9s, gap_p95 2-5s on every file), so cutting on the latest such gap keeps
chunks long (≈ same decode count) while never splitting an utterance. Only the
rare continuous-speech window (longest_speech up to 234s) lacks a band gap and
falls back to a full 30s stride. This is orthogonal to the decode call — it
changes WHERE audio is cut, not how it is decoded — so it composes with any
search/prompt lever later.
hypothesis:
Cutting each window on input-detected silence instead of re-decoding the
tail of a mid-speech cut removes the seam itself: the next window no longer
starts mid-word (seam substitution, the dominant 56% axis) and the cross-seam
re-decode that re-forms verbatim loops on 1065/8016 (the two repeated_text
guard violations, iter_021) can no longer fire, since the boundary now lands
in silence with nothing to re-decode.

capability_investigated:
The raw audio signal as it enters processor()'s feature extractor — specifically
the absence of any spectral pre-emphasis stage. Whisper's WhisperFeatureExtractor
does STFT -> mel -> fixed log offset with no first-difference / high-band lift,
unlike the classical ASR front-end. All prior acoustic probes (iter_014/015/022)
only rescaled amplitude (level), never the spectrum.
what_i_learned:
The feature extractor applies no pre-emphasis, so the input spectrum passes
through unwhitened. On narrowband call-center audio (high-frequency rolloff)
the consonant cues that disambiguate Korean homophones reach the encoder
attenuated — a spectral, not amplitude, axis. This is an input-side acoustic
lever fully reachable on the frozen surface (plain numpy on `audio` before
processor()), distinct from every level-based acoustic probe, with zero extra
decode cost and no effect on windowing/coverage.
hypothesis:
Apply first-difference pre-emphasis (coef 0.97) once over the whole file before
feature extraction. Lifting the high band the phone audio rolls off should
sharpen consonant discrimination and reduce substitution (dominant 56% axis,
length_ratio already healthy 0.96), without the deletion/coverage regression
that sank input-segmentation work (iter_023).

capability_investigated:
generate()'s num_hypotheses on the deterministic beam_size=5 first-pass
decode (iter_011 found it returns the full score-ranked N-best beam list as
parallel sequences_ids/scores), and how the _decode_window degeneracy escape
consumes it — currently it reads only sequences_ids[0] and on failure jumps
straight to topk=0 temperature sampling.
what_i_learned:
The 5 beams the search already completes are thrown away except the argmax,
so a window whose top beam is a repetition loop or low-confidence hypothesis
pays a full sampling re-decode even when a sibling beam (same deterministic
search, on-distribution) already passes the compression+logprob gate. The
N-best is therefore a cost-free degeneracy escape that strictly precedes the
sampling branch iter_005/019 identified as the hallucination/over-generation
source — sampling now fires only when ALL 5 completed beams are degenerate.
hypothesis:
Request num_hypotheses=5 on the beam pass and select the highest-ranked beam
passing the health checks before any temperature escalation. This removes the
sampling-induced insertions on the repeated_text focus files (1065, 8016) and
on low-confidence windows without touching coverage, prompt, or acoustics —
an architectural change to the fallback, not a new parameter value.

capability_investigated:
The raw-audio input path into processor()'s WhisperFeatureExtractor, composing
its two independently-validated un-conditioned acoustic surfaces: the absent
pre-emphasis stage (iter_024, spectral whitening / high-band lift) and the
absent amplitude normalization (iter_014/015, fixed log-mel offset passes raw
level through). Studied whether the two stages compose cleanly when chained.
what_i_learned:
The two front-end gaps are orthogonal and order-dependent: pre-emphasis is a
first-difference filter that itself changes the signal's peak, so amplitude
normalization must run AFTER it to set the level the encoder actually sees.
Both are pure numpy on `audio` before processor(), so they chain with zero
extra decode cost and no effect on the timestamp-seek windowing — unlike the
earlier level compositions (iter_015/022) which paired level with a TEXTUAL
lever (prev-text drift / glossary noise), this pairing keeps both acoustic
gains with no decode-side coupling to regress.
hypothesis:
Apply pre-emphasis (a=0.97) then peak-normalize to 0.95 off the 99.9th
percentile, once per file before feature extraction. iter_024 (sub +0.04 /
hal +0.09) and iter_014/015 (sub +0.04 / hal +0.09) each improved the
dominant substitution axis on quiet narrowband phone audio via independent
mechanisms (spectrum vs level); composing them should stack on substitution
(56%, length_ratio healthy 0.96) without the textual-lever coupling that sank
prior compositions.

capability_investigated:
The transcript-assembly stage `" ".join(texts)` (iter_021's mapped-but-untouched
surface): the joined word stream as the place where per-window verbatim
repetition loops, having passed or evaded the in-window compression+logprob
gate, accumulate into the final return value with no de-duplication.
what_i_learned:
No prior iteration ever transformed the assembled text — every lever acted on
decode inputs, search knobs, or per-window outputs, all of which run BEFORE
concatenation, so a loop that compresses just under 2.4 or re-forms across a
timestamp-seek seam (where window N's tail and window N+1's head repeat the
same span) is structurally unreachable by them and lands verbatim in the
output. The word stream after join exposes both cases in a single pass: a
longest-phrase-first scan for spans repeated >= min_run times is a cost-free,
decode-free assembly-side control distinct from the post-hoc re-decode gate.
hypothesis:
Collapse any 1-12-word phrase repeated >=3x consecutively in the joined
transcript to a single copy. This targets the insertion error on the two
repeated_text guard-violation files (1065, 8016) and the 0.18 repeated rate
the in-search controls (no_repeat_ngram, repetition_penalty, compression gate)
never fully suppressed, without touching substitution or coverage; min_run=3
preserves genuine Korean doublets so it only fires on degeneracy loops.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s writable <|startofprev|> prompt slot used as a TWO-layer context:
a static curated glossary (iter_016) concatenated with rolling clean prev-text
(iter_008), threaded through the mature timestamp-seek loop with a clean-gate.
what_i_learned:
The prompt prefix accepts a composed context — fixed glossary ids + the prior
clean window's encoded text — as one flat list, and the prev-text portion can
be budgeted (PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX - len(glossary)) so the glossary is never
evicted by truncation. The two textual sub-improvers are independent and stack
in a single prompt without extra decode calls; the in-window clean flag is the
natural gate that lets the glossary persist while drifted prev-text is dropped.
hypothesis:
iter_008 (rolling prev-text, biggest sub improver +0.06) regressed from
cold-start and post-degeneracy context voids; iter_016 (static glossary) was
drift-free but isolated. Seeding the glossary on every window fills both voids
while the clean-gate kills iter_008's drift/poison, so the two sub-axis gains
combine without reintroducing either's failure mode.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s no_repeat_ngram_size decoding kwarg applied as a KEPT change on the
mature timestamp-seek pipeline's deterministic beam pass (iter_009 only recorded
that the knob exists as an in-search lever; it was never wired into the actual
decode). Studied where the repeated_text loops on the two guard-violation focus
files sit relative to this knob's per-window scope.
what_i_learned:
The repeated_text guard fires on files (1065, 8016) whose loops compress just
UNDER the 2.4 gate and so never trip the temperature fallback — they are decided
on the first beam pass and survive verbatim into the join. no_repeat_ngram_size
is the only lever that acts at the beam step itself (before a loop finishes
forming), unlike the compression gate (post-hoc, pays a re-decode) and the
assembly-side dedup of iter_021/027 (acts after concatenation). Its scope is
per-window, so it cannot span a seam loop that re-forms across a timestamp-seek
boundary — within-window loops only.
hypothesis:
Banning any repeated 4-gram during the beam search kills the moderate verbatim
loops that slip under the compression gate before they enter the output, clearing
the repeated_text guard violations without the acoustic mix-shift (sub↓ but del↑)
that sank every recent front-end attempt. Size 4 (not 3) spares legitimate short
Korean repeats while still catching the long verbatim loops.
